newsitem.title: USA: NASD censure's Smith Barney, Lehman.
newsitem.headline: NASD censure's Smith Barney, Lehman.

text.p: NASD Regulation Inc said Wednesday it censured and fined Smith Barney and Lehman Brothers $250,000 each and ordered the two firms to pay a combined total of more that $5.6 million in refunds, including interest, to customers overcharged when they redeemed non proprietary mutual funds.
More than 15,700 accounts were affected by the practice of charging commissions where none were allowed, a statement issued by NASD Regulation said.
Later, Lehman Brothers spokesman Chris Cosentino said, "The only thing we want to point out is we are not in this type of retail business any more."
And Smith Barney later issued a statement saying it charged commissions to some clients for mutual fund redemptions from August 1, 1993 through August 28, 1995.

"The error occurred in a mutual fund ticket processing system acquired by Smith Barney during its acquisition of the retail and asset management businesses of Shearson Lehman Brothers in 1993," the statement said. A Smith Barney spokeswoman said "the firm had no intention of overcharging clients."
The overcharges occurred in 7,100 trades out of a total of more than two million trades made during the two year period, Smith Barney said.
Smith Barney said it reimbursed those clients $2.3 million plus $400,000 in interest.
